Thanks Jared — this is clear and a helpful baseline.

High level recommendation from Redwood to align on before we schedule the full run:
1) Calibration run (30m) — synthetic traffic, incremental ramp to 50% target to validate runner config and KV cache behavior.
2) Warm-up (30m) — ramp to 100% but hold for 10m to allow model and KV caches to stabilize.
3) Plateau (60m) — sustained 600 RPS; this is the acceptance window.
4) Cooldown (15m) — step down gracefully.

Acceptance metric we propose to record and share: 99th and 95th latencies during the plateau, CPU/GPU utilization, token throughput, and error rate. For the acceptance confidence window we use a 95% bootstrap across one-hour slices (we call this the "confidence window") — in plain terms we look for stable behavior across three independent 1-hour slices if possible.

Two quick questions for you:
- Are you comfortable with synthetic traffic for calibration/warm-up (we'll use your payloads for plateau)?
- Any PII in the sample payloads that requires redaction for the test environment?

We'll provision a canary run slot on 2028-09-21 02:00-04:00 PDT and follow with the formal plateau test later that day (window TBD). Monica and Ben are cc'd to confirm test config and gather artifacts.

Thanks — I'll follow up with a short runbook and a deliverables checklist.

—Tessa

Subject: Internal: proposed test configuration for Umbra Pay (draft)

Internal notes (do not forward to customer yet):

Proposed Redwood config for the plateau run:
- Model: open-llama-13B-quant-int8 (verified performance profile)
- Batch strategy: continuous dynamic batching with max batch size 128, token-based batching on 512-token window
- KV cache: persisted across requests for plateau; clear before calibration run
- Ramp: 0 -> 50% over 10m (calibration), 50% -> 100% over 20m (warm-up)
- Plateau: 60m sustained at 600 RPS (payload size ~420 tokens average)
- Measurement: collect per-token latency, per-request end-to-end latency, and GPU utilization at 15s granularity
- Acceptance thresholds (proposed internal): 95th <= 220 ms, 99th <= 280 ms, error rate < 0.5% during plateau

Statistical note on confidence window: instead of a single aggregate 99th we compute a 95% bootstrap CI over 1-hour windows and require the upper bound of the CI to be under the customer's SLA. That reduces noise from bursts. We'll include both aggregate percentiles and the CI in the report.

Attach: redwood-calibration-runbook.pdf (draft)

—Monica
